'''''Veronica acinifolia''''', the '''French speedwell''', is an annual [[Flowering plant|flower]] in the family [[Plantaginaceae]] present within a band from Portugal to Britain on the west stretching eastwards far into Asia,<ref name="PoWo"/> with some gaps.

==Description==
A small (to {{Convert|15|cm|abbr=on|disp=or}}), [[Annual plant|annual]], bright blue flowered [[Veronica_(plant)|speedwell]] with an upright stance, covered with glands, with small (to {{Convert|1|cm|4=1|abbr=on|disp=or}} long), broadish leaves whose toothing is weak and blunt (or absent), the leaves becoming smaller upwards through the flowering section where they become small and narrower. The blue flowers are small (2–4 mm), and the fruit (2 x 3–4 mm) has two lobes separated deeply from the top.<ref name="Sell3">{{cite book |title=Flora of Great Britain and Ireland, vol. 3, p. 470 |author=Peter Sell & Gina Murrell}}</ref><ref name="FoT">{{cite book |title=Flora of Turkey and the East Aegean Islands, vol. 6, p. 708 |author=Davis}}</ref>

Photographic examples can be seen on [https://www.inaturalist.org/taxa/336247/browse_photos?quality_grade=research iNaturalist].

==Distribution and habitat==
Its native range is Albania, Altay, Bulgaria, Corsica, Czechoslovakia, East Aegean Islands, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Italy, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Crete, Crimea, Lebanon-Syria, Mongolia, Portugal, Romania, Spain, Switzerland, Turkey, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Xinjiang, Yugoslavia, extinct in Belgium, and introduced into the British Isles.<ref name="PoWo"/>

Its habitat is cultivated ground, damp grassland, ditches, damp paths,<ref name="FEU">{{cite book |title=Flora Europaea, vol. 3, p. 248 |author=Tutin}}</ref> in Turkey from 0 to {{Convert|200|m|abbr=on}}.<ref name="FoT"/>
